title: I took your feedback and kept working on Portal Beasts — new worlds, redesigned beasts, and a new gameplay trailer
author: PortalBeasts
selftext:
Hey everyone!

A while ago, I shared Portal Beasts here, my solo-developed monster-catching action RPG. Some of you tried the demo, asked about the development process, or pointed out things that needed work. I wanted to come back with an update and show where the game is now.

For anyone seeing it for the first time: you directly control your beasts in real-time battles, moving, aiming attacks, and dodging or shielding.

One comment on my previous post pointed out that trees had shadows while the characters and beasts didn’t. That was a fair point, and it led to quite a bit of work on shadows, sprite positioning, and making everything feel like it belongs in the same game.

Here’s what else I’ve been working on:

* **A more consistent color palette.** I reworked environment colors and outlines, then went back over assets where the changes had lost detail or made materials look wrong.
* **New worlds.** Volcanic forests, tropical islands, and a swamp with shallow water you can wade through.
* **New and redesigned beasts**, including new evolutions and more complete directional animations.
* **Combat improvements.** Clearer hit effects, adjustments to hit detection and movement speed, and more work on how enemies choose their attacks and use defensive abilities.
* **Beasts helping outside combat.** Water beasts can pull your raft between islands.
* **UI and controls.** A revised interface, remappable controls, and an optional quick-cast mode.

I’ve put together a new 90-second gameplay trailer showing the current version. It includes areas being developed for the full game; the free demo covers the town, Mosswood, and Hollowwood, up to your first Portal Ranger exam.

I’m still using Godot, with AI-assisted coding and art tools alongside Aseprite and purchased assets. Getting the results to work together has meant a lot of testing and reworking things.

I’d love to hear how this compares with the earlier version. Does the art feel more consistent now, and can you clearly follow what’s happening during combat?

[**Play the free demo on Steam**](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal_Beasts_Demo/)

Thanks for taking another look!  
Lasse
